title: Swedbank Mobile App Start Page
subtitle: A service design concept, not a screen redesign

slides.title: Swedbank Mobile App Start Page
slides.standfirst: A conceptual design deliberately scoped beyond a native screen redesign — anchored on financial overview, structured by the Swedish monthly income cycle, and treating advice as a service moment rather than an advertising slot.

bullets.text: UX Director, conceptual design
Financial overview and budget management
Swedbank's values: Open, Sharing, Caring

slides.notes: The scoping decision is the first thing worth defending: this was framed as service design before any screen was drawn, and that choice shapes everything including the validation plan.

slides.title: A bank start page serves two agendas that usually undermine each other

bullets.text: A small set of recurring questions: what is my position, will I have money left, what should I do next.
The same surface has to introduce products at the right moment.

callout.text: The second agenda degrades the first, and the start page becomes a promotional space users learn to scroll past.

slides.notes: "Learn to scroll past" is the failure mode to name. It is not that users dislike offers; it is that they train themselves to ignore a region of the screen.

slides.title: Where the journey starts today
slides.standfirst: The concept begins from the existing app — the login, and the surface a customer lands on when they open it to answer one small question.

bullets.text: Customers arrive with a question, not with an appetite for browsing.
So the start page is judged on how fast it answers, not on how much it contains.
Anything occupying that surface has to earn its place against the question.

slides.title: The persona is not a click, it is a relationship
slides.standfirst: Someone who wants to make thoughtful decisions, always have money left, is open to advice — and is a loyal customer holding few banking relationships.

bullets.text: Decisions are considered, not impulsive.
The goal is to always have money left.
Which is an opportunity and a liability at once.
So a misjudged offer costs more than it earns.

figure.text: The start page is not competing for a click. It is maintaining a long relationship.

slides.notes: The loyalty point is the commercial argument for restraint. A customer with few banking relationships is expensive to annoy.

slides.title: Five pillars
slides.standfirst: Content, behaviour, commerce, structure and rhythm — decided before any layout.
slides.notes: Naming the commercial requirement as a pillar rather than hiding it is what makes the rest of the concept honest.

slides.notes: Pillars three and five interact: the offer is timed to the income cycle, which is what converts a pitch into a service moment.

slides.title: Swedish salaries arrive monthly, so the month is the unit of comprehension
slides.standfirst: Not the day, and not the week. A budget question is only answerable against the period the money arrived for.

bullets.text: "Will I have money left" is a question about a month, asked on an arbitrary day within it.
A timeline structured on the income cycle answers it without the customer doing arithmetic.
And it gives offers a natural, non-intrusive moment: the point in the cycle where the answer changes.

callout.lead: Which is why the timeline is a pillar rather than a component
callout.text: It is the temporal structure of the page, not a widget on it.

slides.notes: This is the best idea in the concept. Spend time here — it is culturally specific, defensible, and it produces both the layout and the commercial timing.

slides.title: Advice as a service moment, not an advertising slot
slides.standfirst: The pitch is earned by delivering genuine financial overview first, and timed to the monthly income cycle so the recommendation arrives when it is contextually useful.

bullets.text: Answer the customer's question before making an offer.
To the point in the income cycle where the offer is actually relevant.
So the offer reads as the bank helping the customer, not selling to them.
In consultation with the sales department, not around them.

slides.title: Everyday interaction, made playful

figure.caption: Engaging and playful daily interaction — one of three stated conditions

slides.notes: Playful has a cost: it depends entirely on charge categorisation being right. Say the dependency out loud rather than showing this as free delight.

slides.title: Three things stated as prerequisites before further development

cards.title: Engaging and playful daily interaction
cards.text: Requires desk research and consultation to get everyday charge categorization right. Without accurate categories, the playfulness is noise.

cards.title: Relevant sales pitches
cards.text: Developed in consultation with the sales department, so the offer reads as the bank helping the customer rather than selling to them.

cards.title: Consistency
cards.text: Achieved by working within Swedbank's existing front-end style guide rather than around it — a concept that ignores the style guide is a concept that cannot ship.

slides.notes: These are conditions, not caveats. Each one is a dependency on someone outside the design team, and naming them is what makes the concept actionable.

slides.title: Making commercial content welcome
slides.standfirst: A start page carrying sales pitches is normally experienced as a tax on the customer's own task.

bullets.text: The persona is open to advice — and also loyal and financially cautious.
Which means a misjudged offer costs more than it earns.
Earn the pitch by delivering genuine overview first, and time it to the income cycle so it arrives when it is useful.

callout.text: Treating the brief as a service design problem meant the concept could not be validated by screen testing alone. That is why it ships with a staged research plan rather than a claim of validation.

slides.notes: The second half is the more interesting half. Widening the scope bought a better concept and cost the ability to validate it cheaply — an honest trade, stated as one.

slides.title: Commercial content is welcome when it arrives inside a rhythm the customer already lives in
slides.standfirst: The usual fix for an ignored promotional slot is to make it louder. The better fix is to make it timely — which requires knowing the customer's cycle, not their segment.

callout.lead: Which is why this could not stay a screen redesign
callout.text: Timing an offer to the income cycle is a service decision. No amount of layout work gets you there.

slides.notes: End on this. It justifies the scoping decision made on slide one, which closes the deck's own loop.
